conflicts.topic: What the step / hero part is called

positions.quote: step(10, P4, "Remove intake duct",
Remove the intake hose/resonator assembly.
Step: "Remove the air intake hose."
"component": "Air inlet duct, IAT connector, clamps, grommet"
"Intake hose",

conflicts.contradiction: Four different names for the hero part: 'intake duct' (guide title), 'intake hose/resonator assembly' (guide action), 'air intake hose' (prompt), 'Air inlet duct … grommet' (manifest), 'Intake hose' (shot list). The prompt's own hero is a single hose, the guide's removal target is a hose/resonator ASSEMBLY.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Pick the one canonical customer-facing name for the hero part, and say whether it is a hose, a duct, or a hose+resonator assembly. (Feeds CF-03.)

conflicts.topic: Retaining grommet — required by the step, banned by the prompt, split between manifest and shot list

positions.quote: Release the intake assembly from its retaining grommet.
engine cover, hose grommet, resonator, any second or red locking feature on the connector
"Retaining grommet"
Every callout target below is a component the step's own text names; none is added by us.

conflicts.contradiction: The guide's fourth action is to release the assembly from its retaining grommet, and the old manifest lists 'Retaining grommet' as a callout target. The prompt lists 'hose grommet' under MUST NOT SHOW (leave out entirely, do not substitute). The shot list has no grommet target at all, although its own header says every target is a component the step text names. An image that obeys the prompt cannot show, let alone call out, the part the guide's action 4 acts on. (Guide step 2 also says 'retaining grommets', plural, for the engine cover — a different part.)
conflicts.decisionRequired: Decide: is the step-10 grommet shown (and called out), or is action 4 left un-illustrated? If shown, the prompt's MUST NOT SHOW must be amended and evidence for the grommet must exist. If not shown, the manifest's callout target must be dropped.

conflicts.topic: Resonator — named in the step text, banned by the prompt

positions.quote: Remove the intake hose/resonator assembly.
MUST NOT SHOW (leave these out entirely, do not substitute): engine cover, hose grommet, resonator,
No seam, joint or ring between the two sections.

conflicts.contradiction: The guide's last action removes a 'hose/resonator assembly'; the prompt requires the hero to be ONE hose with no seam and forbids the resonator entirely.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Decide whether the resonator is part of the pictured assembly. This must be settled together with CF-01 (what the hero is) before any evidence ledger row for the hero can be written.

conflicts.topic: Callout target set and order (manifest vs shot list vs step text vs callout spec)

positions.quote: "IAT electrical connector",
"Clamp at the throttle body",
"Clamp at the air-cleaner housing",
"IAT connector",
"Air-box clamp",
Four actions on one assembly: IAT clip, two clamps, then lift the hose out.
Components the step text itself names, in the order they should be called out.

conflicts.contradiction: Manifest targets: IAT electrical connector / Clamp at the throttle body / Clamp at the air-cleaner housing / Retaining grommet (no hose). Shot-list targets: IAT connector / Throttle-body clamp / Air-box clamp / Intake hose (no grommet). The recovered callout spec says targets are components the step text names, in the step text's order — the step text names five things (IAT connector, throttle-body clamp, air-cleaner-housing clamp, retaining grommet, intake hose/resonator assembly). The two lists agree on three, disagree on the fourth and omit the fifth/fourth respectively, and use different wording for the same targets.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Decide the final callout list (count ≤ 6 per the callout rules), its order, and the exact label wording. Until then no callout geometry can be requested.

positions.quote: Disconnect the IAT electrical connector. Loosen the clamp at the throttle body. Loosen the clamp at the air-cleaner housing. Release the intake assembly from its retaining grommet. Remove the intake hose/resonator assembly.
Four actions on one assembly: IAT clip, two clamps, then lift the hose out.

conflicts.contradiction: The guide step has five actions; the shot list's rationale counts four and omits the grommet release. It also calls the connector an 'IAT clip' where the guide says 'IAT electrical connector'.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Confirm the number of actions the single image must support (four or five) — a restatement of CF-02 for the shot list's 'why'.

positions.quote: Loosen the clamp at the air-cleaner housing.
"_needs": "Air-inlet system from the throttle body back to the air-cleaner housing, all clamps and the connector in view."
Air box: a low rounded box with a ribbed lid and an inlet collar on its engine-side end
"Air-box clamp",

conflicts.contradiction: Guide and manifest say 'air-cleaner housing'; prompt and shot list say 'air box'. Nothing surviving says they are the same component or fixes the customer-facing label.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Confirm they are the same component and fix ONE label (the label is shown on the image and in the legend).

conflicts.topic: Clamps — step says loosen them, prompt forbids drawing the loosening hardware

positions.quote: Loosen the clamp at the throttle body.
Do NOT show the screw, screw head, screw housing, or any tightening hardware
all clamps and the connector in view

conflicts.contradiction: The action is loosening a clamp; the prompt requires plain smooth bands with the tightening side turned away, so the part a reader must act on is hidden, while the manifest asks for all clamps 'in view'.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Decide whether clamp hardware may be shown (needs fastener-position / fastener-head-type evidence — a safety-critical ledger attribute) or the callout is allowed to point at a band whose loosening point is not visible.

conflicts.topic: IAT connector — 'disconnect' vs 'no release/locking features'; 'partly hidden' vs 'in view' vs a callout that must touch it

positions.quote: Disconnect the IAT electrical connector.
Plain block only: no release tab, no pins, no colours, no locking features.
partly hidden behind the hose edge
all clamps and the connector in view
someone must confirm each arrow points at its component

conflicts.contradiction: The step has the reader disconnect the connector; the prompt draws it with no release feature at all and partly hidden. The manifest wants it in view and the callout rules require a reviewer to confirm each arrow lands on the component it names, which a partly hidden, featureless block makes unverifiable.
conflicts.decisionRequired: Decide the minimum visibility of the connector and whether any release feature may be drawn (needs release-mechanism-geometry evidence if so). Where it sits on the hose is also stated only by the prompt — see MISSING evidence M-02.
